name: instance_guard
description: Duplicate-SDK-instance guard, shared by both SDKs. TS source: sdk/src/proxy/instance-guard.ts (Symbol.for global slot). Python twin: sdk-python/obsvr/instance_guard.py (a sys.modules slot - a module-level variable would not survive the very duplication this guards against). Both suites (sdk/tests/unit/instance-guard.test.ts, sdk-python/tests/test_instance_guard.py) drive these sequences and must reach the same outcome. The SDK can appear in one process twice - installed directly and again as a transitive dependency - and two copies would each poll, each wrap, and each emit, producing duplicate evidence for a single call.

semantics.first_claim_wins: the first copy to initialize governs; later copies yield
semantics.reinit_is_not_duplication: the governing copy re-initializing (new config) keeps governing and logs nothing
semantics.log_once: a yielding copy logs exactly once, at init - a duplicate install is one problem, not one per call
semantics.yield_means_passthrough: a yielded copy does not poll and does not wrap; clients wrapped through it are NOT governed, which is why the log names the fix (deduplicate the dependency)
semantics.incumbent_keeps_the_slot: even when the incumbent is an older version; that case is called out in the log rather than triggering a takeover, because taking over mid-process would leave the incumbent's already-wrapped clients governed by a released instance

cases.desc: one copy, one claim: it governs and logs nothing
a second copy finds the slot taken, logs once, and does not govern
the yielded copy re-initializing does not turn one duplicate install into a stream of warnings
re-initializing the governing copy with new config is not duplication
a newer copy still yields to an older incumbent, and the log says the governing copy is older
the older-version note appears only when it is true
